## Introduction

**dimsprepr** provides a complete, reproducible preprocessing pipeline for
direct-injection mass spectrometry (DIMS) metabolomics data. It covers blank
filtering, missing-value handling, QC-based signal-drift and batch
correction, imputation, normalization, transformation, quality filtering,
and scaling, all orchestrated through a single function call. Its quality
control steps follow the QComics guidelines (González-Domínguez et al.,
2024), and it offers the outlier-robust drift correction methods of Vynck et
al. (2026).

## The example data

```{r setup}
library(dimsprepr)

data(dims_data)
data(dims_metadata)

dim(dims_data)
table(dims_metadata$Group, dims_metadata$Batch)
head(dims_metadata)
```

`dims_data` is a simulated 60-injection, 80-feature matrix in two batches.
Pooled QC samples open and close each batch and recur every 6th injection,
the layout QC-based drift correction needs. Zeros mark values below the
detection limit.

## Run the full pipeline

`run_DIpreprocess()` executes all steps in a fixed, validated order:

1. input validation;
2. sample removal (listed outliers, and procedural blanks after blank
   filtering when `blank_types` is given);
3. missing-value handling: removal of samples with abnormally low detection
   rates, then the modified 80% rule;
4. drift and batch correction, on data that still contain missing values;
5. imputation;
6. normalization;
7. transformation;
8. quality filtering (QC-RSD on measured values, then variance, both on
   unscaled data);
9. scaling into a NONPLS and a PLS branch;
10. replicate merging.

```{r pipeline}
result <- run_DIpreprocess(
  x                = dims_data,
  metadata         = dims_metadata,
  normalize_method = "pqn_group",
  transform_method = "log10",
  verbose          = FALSE
)

result
summary(result)
```

The result keeps the data after each step, the final matrices for the two
scaling branches, and a log of the dimensions:

```{r inspect}
dim(result$data_nonpls)   # auto-scaled: PCA, clustering, univariate tests
dim(result$data_pls)      # Pareto-scaled: PLS-DA / OPLS-DA
head(result$features_final)
```

## Diagnostic plots

`plot_beforeafter()` shows features along the injection order, with a
LOESS trend through the QC samples. Given a pipeline result, it compares the
data before and after drift correction:

```{r plot-drift}
plot_beforeafter(result, plot_what = c("mz_0002", "mz_0015"))
```

`plot_dist_beforeafter()` compares distributions, here the imputed raw
intensities with the final auto-scaled data:

```{r plot-dist}
plot_dist_beforeafter(result, n_random = 15)
```

## Choosing a drift correction method

`drift_method` selects the correction applied by
`run_driftBatchCorrect()`:

* `"QCRSC"` (default): a smoothing spline through the QC samples (Kirwan et
  al., 2013);
* `"rLOESS"`, `"rGAM"`, `"tGAM"`: outlier-robust trend models (Vynck et al.,
  2026), which are not pulled off course by an occasional aberrant QC
  injection. rGAM and tGAM need the **mgcv** package and can also use the
  biological samples, with a lower weight, to estimate the drift;
* `"ComBat"`: batch offsets only, without QCs (needs **sva**);
* `"none"`: skip the step.

Extra settings go in `drift_args`. Here, rGAM uses the biological samples
with a 5:1 QC-to-sample weighting:

```{r robust, eval = requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)}
robust <- run_DIpreprocess(
  dims_data[, 1:20], dims_metadata,
  drift_method = "rGAM",
  drift_args   = list(sample_weight = 0.2),
  verbose      = FALSE
)
robust$dimensions
```

Features that cannot be corrected in every batch, because they have fewer
than `min_QC` measured QC values there, are removed by default
(`remove_uncorrected = TRUE`).

## QComics quality checks

* **Blanks**: with `blank_types = "Blank"`, features whose signal in study
  samples is below 3 times their blank signal are flagged as potential
  contaminants, those with an unstable blank signal (RSD > 15%) are removed,
  and the blank injections are dropped (`run_filterblank()`).
* **Failed injections**: samples whose detection rate is abnormally low
  within their group are removed (`missing_sample_iqr`, default `3`; see
  `result$samples_removed`).
* **Truly absent data**: with `missing_absent_threshold = 0.7`, features
  missing in more than 70% of a group are kept as zeros in that group
  instead of being removed.

## Using individual functions

Each step is also available as a standalone function. Note that drift
correction runs before imputation, as QC-based correction ignores missing
values while imputed QC values would bias it.

```{r steps}
filt  <- run_filtermissing(dims_data, dims_metadata, threshold = 0.2,
                           sample_iqr = 3, verbose = FALSE)
corr  <- run_driftBatchCorrect(filt$data, filt$metadata, verbose = FALSE)
imp   <- run_mvimpute(corr$data, method = 0.2, verbose = FALSE)
norm  <- run_normalize(imp$data, filt$metadata, method = "pqn_group",
                       verbose = FALSE)
rsd   <- run_filterRSD(norm$data, filt$metadata, max_rsd = 0.3, verbose = FALSE)
trans <- run_transform(rsd$data, method = "log10", verbose = FALSE)
varf  <- run_filtervariance(trans$data, percentile = 10, verbose = FALSE)
sc    <- run_scale(varf$data, method = "auto", verbose = FALSE)

filt
corr
sc
```

## Comparing preprocessing strategies

Supply vectors to `normalize_method`, `transform_method`, `scale_nonpls`, or
`scale_pls` to compute all combinations. Steps 1 to 5 run only once, and
normalization, transformation, and filtering run once per
normalize x transform pair:

```{r multi}
multi <- run_DIpreprocess(
  x                = dims_data,
  metadata         = dims_metadata,
  normalize_method = c("median", "pqn_group"),
  transform_method = c("log10", "ln"),
  verbose          = FALSE
)
multi
```

## References

González-Domínguez, A., Estanyol-Torres, N., Brunius, C., Landberg, R., &
González-Domínguez, R. (2024). QComics: Recommendations and guidelines for
robust, easily implementable and reportable quality control of metabolomics
data. *Analytical Chemistry*, 96(3), 1064-1072.
<https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.3c03660>

Kirwan, J.A., Broadhurst, D.I., Davidson, R.L., & Viant, M.R. (2013).
Characterising and correcting batch variation in an automated direct
infusion mass spectrometry (DIMS) metabolomics workflow. *Analytical and
Bioanalytical Chemistry*, 405(15), 5147-5157.
<https://doi.org/10.1007/s00216-013-6856-7>

Vynck, M., Vangeenderhuysen, P., De Paepe, E., Nawrot, T., Plekhova, V., &
Vanhaecke, L. (2026). Robust metabolomics data normalization across scales
and experimental designs. *Analytical Chemistry*, 98(24), 17627-17637.
<https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.5c06841>
